findings.title: Config never reaches `WorkflowNavigator` or `ConsistencyChecker` — the "both surfaces inherit it without per-surface work" goal is false
findings.description: The gate is config-driven (`workflow.review_enabled`, `review_threshold`, per-transition overrides), but both target classes are constructed with no config today: `new WorkflowNavigator()` in `packages/cli/src/commands/next.ts:26` and `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:119`, and `new WorkflowNavigator()` / `new ConsistencyChecker(introspector)` in `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts`. `getNext(project: ProjectData)` and `deriveSliceStatus()` read only `ProjectData` + the filesystem (`packages/core/src/introspection/WorkflowNavigator.ts:83`, `:446`), and `ProjectData` (`packages/core/src/types/project.ts`) carries no config fields. Config lives in `ConfigManager`, which every current call site constructs separately (e.g. `check.ts:134-141`). The document says the gate is "inherited by both surfaces … without per-surface work," but wiring `ConfigManager` into the navigator and checker (or threading a resolved config object through the constructors of `next.ts`, `status.ts`, `workflowTools.ts`, and `check.ts`) **is** per-surface work, and the document never states where that happens or whether `ConfigManager` should be injected. This is a load-bearing plumbing decision left implicit; the initative-plan framing ("mirroring the existing `workflow.auto_advance` / `workflow.auto_fix` knobs") is misleading because neither of those keys is actually read by the navigator today — `auto_advance` behavior was explicitly deferred (`packages/core/src/config/ConfigKeys.ts:26`, DEVLOG "behavior deferred").

findings.title: Gate logic placed inside `deriveSliceStatus()` will be silently swallowed by its broad `catch`
findings.description: `deriveSliceStatus()` wraps its entire body in `try { … } catch { return base; }` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:456-498`, catch at `:494`), where `base.status === 'no-active-slice'`. The document requires the gate to treat a review file that "exists but cannot be parsed (malformed YAML, unreadable encoding, permission error)" as `UNKNOWN` and to "name the parse failure explicitly." If the review read happens inside `deriveSliceStatus` (as the document specifies — "Extend `deriveSliceStatus()` to set these values when gate conditions apply"), any thrown error collapses the whole slice to `no-active-slice` — a silent failure, and the exact opposite of the stated fail-fast/`UNKNOWN` behavior. The document does not say how the existing swallowing catch is restructured or that it must be narrowed before adding this logic.

findings.title: The existing frontmatter parser cannot satisfy the stated "name the parse failure explicitly" requirement
findings.description: `parseFrontmatter` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/frontmatterParser.ts`) "Never throws — returns `{ found: false, data: {} }` on any error," including `readFile` failure (permission, encoding). It therefore cannot distinguish "no frontmatter block" from "file unreadable," which the document's file-read-failure mode requires it to report distinctly. It is also a flat `key: value` line scanner (`FrontmatterData = Record<string, string>`), so the nested `criteria` map and any multi-line YAML in the Squadron-300 schema will not parse. The document's plan to "carry `criteria` and `provenance` as opaque fields … preserved for downstream tools" is not achievable through this parser, and the parse-failure-detection behavior needs its own mechanism rather than reuse of `parseFrontmatter`.

findings.title: "Current transition" is never defined — the per-gate config has no resolution rule
findings.description: The per-gate config keys are `pre-slice-plan`, `pre-tasks`, `pre-implementation`, `pre-advance`, but these names do not correspond to anything in the cascade, which branches on `slice.status ∈ {needs-design, needs-tasks, in-implementation, complete}` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:212-278`). The document repeatedly refers to "the gate for the current transition" (e.g. "When … no gate is configured for the current transition, the status goes directly from `complete` to advance") without ever stating how the navigator determines which transition it is currently in, or how a slice that is `pending-review` for answer `pre-tasks` differs from one at `pre-advance`. Without this mapping, `deriveSliceStatus()` cannot select a `reviewType` or threshold, so the commit's central mechanism is unspecified.

findings.title: Default `review_unknown_as = "fail"` contradicts the "locked" v1 threshold decision in the source input
findings.description: The source note's "Decisions already locked (do not re-open)" section states: "**v1 threshold is conservative** — `verdict != FAIL` passes." The architecture instead defaults `review_unknown_as = "fail"`, so `UNKNOWN` (and absent verdict) blocks by default — i.e. `verdict == UNKNOWN` does **not** pass. The document asserts it is building on locked decisions but flips a default the input marks as settled, without noting the change. Whichever is intended, the divergence must be reconciled with the initiative-plan wording before implementation, because it changes the default behavior for every verdict-less review artifact (which the input explicitly calls "the *normal* v1 case," since no template emits a score/verdict yet).

findings.title: `review_unknown_as` / threshold vocabulary is under-specified and mixes two value spaces
findings.description: The verdict vocabulary is `PASS | CONCERNS | FAIL | UNKNOWN`, but `review_unknown_as` is written as `"concern"` (singular) in Technical Considerations and `"fail"` in Config keys — is it a verdict value, a threshold value, or its own enum? No enumeration is given. Meanwhile the threshold clears on "`review_threshold = "concerns"` or lower" while the per-gate example uses `threshold = "pass"`, so "concerns is lower than pass" but "concerns" is the *more permissive* setting — the "or lower" phrasing is backwards from how a threshold normally reads and will confuse readers and code alike. Additionally, the `pending-review` definition says a verdict of `UNKNOWN` "treats it as pending" (a state), while the Verdict handling section says `UNKNOWN` is mapped to `CONCERNS` and compared to the threshold (not a state) — two different outcomes for the same input. Per the project rule "define comparison values once," these constants and their semantics need a single canonical definition (enum) and one clear precedence table.

findings.title: The ConsistencyChecker rule cannot see the new slot or the config it depends on
findings.description: The rule is gated on `review_enabled = true`, but `ConsistencyChecker` (`packages/core/src/introspection/ConsistencyChecker.ts`) is constructed with only an `IArtifactIntrospector` and receives `ProjectData` — no `ConfigManager` or config value (same gap as the navigator). Separately, its `safeDetectDocuments` helper narrows the detector result to `{ taskFile, sliceDesign }` (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:1053-1061`), so a new `review` field on `DocumentDetectionResult` will not be visible to the checker unless that helper and the private `checkSlice` signature are also changed — neither is mentioned. The document describes the rule as "a new `ConsistencyFinding` rule" but the actual integration points (config access + widened detection result) are not addressed.

findings.title: New slice statuses will surface on `cf status` / `workflow_status` with no update to those surfaces
findings.description: The document adds `pending-review` / `review-failed` to `SliceStatus` and justifies it as "the visualizer and runners can act on them." But `SliceStatus` flows into `getStatus()` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:50-79`), which is consumed by `cf status` (`packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:135`) and the MCP `workflow_status` tool — whose description hard-codes the old enum: "(needs-design, needs-tasks, in-implementation, complete)" (`packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts`). Those call sites also instantiate `WorkflowNavigator` without config, so they would either miss the new states or (once config is threaded in) start emitting them. The document claims the gate routes through `workflow_next`/`workflow_check` only; it does not account for the third surface (`workflow_status`/`cf status`) that shares `deriveSliceStatus()`, nor state that the MCP tool description must be updated. This is exactly the "interfaces described the same way wherever they appear" concern.

findings.title: `Related Work` claims "no 160 interfaces change" while the design changes a 160 interface
findings.description: "Inititiative 240 is purely additive to 160's infrastructure; no 160 interfaces change." But `DocumentDetectionResult` (`packages/core/src/introspection/types.ts:67-73`) is a 160-defined interface (it is the return type of `IArtifactIntrospector.detectDocuments`, `interfaces.ts:26`), and the design adds a `review` slot to it. Because its fields are currently all required non-optional (`sliceDesign: string | null`, etc.), adding a required `review` field is a breaking change for every implementer/consumer of that interface (`ArtifactIntrospector`, all test doubles, and `summarize()`), not purely additive. The document should either make the new field optional or stop claiming no interface changes.

findings.title: Per-transition `review_gates` config machinery is built before the gate logic and largely for a deferred feature
findings.description: Slice 1 adds "the three global config keys **and per-gate override structure**," which the document itself flags will likely require extending `ConfigKeyDefinition` to "support nested shapes" (an interface with `type: 'string' | 'boolean' | 'number'` and no nested-table support — `ConfigKeys.ts:1-7`). For v1, however, only the four slice-level transitions matter, and the `pre-slice-plan` gate in the override example is explicitly deferred to a later slice ("Initiative-level gating (v1 deferred)"). The document therefore front-loads a config-schema extension (and the design-time decision about flat dotted keys vs. nested tables) to serve a capability v1 does not implement, while the transitions that *are* implemented need only a global threshold plus at most a per-reviewType setting. The heavier nested-gate machinery is the proportionate-vs-overbuilt tension the document should resolve by naming what can be cut or deferred to the slice that actually consumes it.

findings.title: "Lexicographically last = most recent" tie-break is unsupported by the stated naming scheme
findings.description: The document resolves multiple matches by taking "the lexicographically last filename (most recent by sort order)." The stated convention `NNN-review.{reviewType}.*.md` (example: `210-review.code.github-copilot-vs-code-ide-support.md`) embeds a descriptive name, not a date — so sort order reflects the descriptive suffix alphabetically, not chronology. "Most recent" is therefore not derivable from the name as documented, making the selection arbitrary-but-deterministic in a way that may silently pick the wrong review. It also conflicts with the existing detector's handling: `matchFiles` sorts ascending and `documentDetector.ts` takes `[0]` for `sliceDesign`, so the same detector would use opposite "first/last" conventions within one function. Either the naming must include a sortable timestamp (the frontmatter regex allows an optional `-\d+` suffix) or the tie-break must be re-specified (e.g., highest `dateUpdated`), and this should be stated as the rule rather than asserted as a property of the filename.

findings.title: New `recommendation` tokens mix machine values into a human-sentence field
findings.description: `NextAction.recommendation` is currently free-form human prose ("Continue implementation — 3 tasks remaining"). The design adds machine tokens (`"review"`, `"blocked"`) that downstream Amoeba is told to match on ("Depends on CF returning structured `recommendation` values with a stable vocabulary"). A consumer keying on exact string equality against a field otherwise used for display text is a fragile coupling; the document should state whether a separate structured field (e.g., an action kind) is warranted rather than overloading `recommendation`, and note that existing consumers that print `recommendation` verbatim will render `"review"`/`"blocked"` as bare words.
